subject: paediatrics
title: Neonatal Hypothermia, Retinopathy and Necrotising Enterocolitis

steps.tx: Premature and low birth weight infants are profoundly vulnerable to **neonatal environmental hypothermia**. Due to a high ratio of body surface area to mass, deficient insulating subcutaneous fat, non-keratinized thin skin, and minimal brown fat stores, heat loss exceeds metabolic production unless strict environmental temperature control is maintained in an incubator.
steps.say: High surface area and deficient subcutaneous fat make preterm infants highly prone to hypothermia.

vis.alt: Preterm infant losing heat by radiation, conduction, convection and evaporation in an incubator with servo-controlled skin probe
vis.caption: Preterm infant losing heat by radiation, conduction, convection and evaporation in an incubator with servo-controlled skin probe. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Vascular proliferative disorder of the developing retina in preterm neonates is **retinopathy of prematurity**. Incomplete retinal vascularization at birth makes peripheral retinal capillaries exquisitely sensitive to hyperoxia. Exposure to unmonitored supplemental oxygen downregulates vascular endothelial growth factor, arresting vessel growth; subsequent relative hypoxia triggers pathological neovascularization, vitreous traction, and retinal detachment.
steps.say: Retinopathy of prematurity is driven by hyperoxia followed by hypoxia, stimulating retinal neovascularization.

rows: Flat white line separating vascular and avascular retina
Demarcation line gains height and width above retina
Fibrovascular tufts grow into vitreous body
Tractional detachment sparing or involving fovea
Complete funnel detachment causing irreversible blindness

steps.tx: Universal screening criteria target all preterm infants born at or before thirty-four weeks gestation or weighing **under two thousand grams**. Fundoscopic examination using an indirect ophthalmoscope is performed at four weeks of postnatal age or thirty-one to thirty-two weeks postmenstrual age. The presence of plus disease, characterized by arteriolar tortuosity and venular dilatation in the posterior pole, indicates aggressive progression.
steps.say: Screening is performed at four weeks postnatal age in preterms under two thousand grams.

left.title: Screening Indications
points: High-risk preterms with unstable clinical course

right.title: Plus Disease Features
points: Severe dilatation of posterior pole venules
Mandates urgent laser or anti-VEGF therapy

steps.tx: The most common life-threatening gastrointestinal medical emergency in the neonatal intensive care unit is **necrotising enterocolitis**. Pathogenesis involves a triad of intestinal mucosal immaturity, formula feeding that introduces antigens and promotes bacterial proliferation, and ischemic mucosal injury following perinatal hypoxia. Translocation of gas-producing bacteria triggers progressive bowel wall necrosis.
steps.say: Necrotising enterocolitis results from bowel immaturity, formula feeding, and ischemic mucosal injury.

rows: Deficient peristalsis and thin mucosal barrier
Hypoxic shunting away from splanchnic bed
Judicious fluid management and antenatal steroids

steps.tx: Clinical severity and therapeutic decision-making are guided by **modified Bell staging criteria**. Stage one represents suspected disease with feeding intolerance, abdominal distension, and occult microscopic blood in stool. Stage two indicates definite disease with absent bowel sounds, abdominal tenderness, and metabolic acidosis. Stage three designates advanced disease with peritonitis and septic shock.
steps.say: Bell staging categorizes necrotising enterocolitis from mild feeding intolerance to perforation and shock.

rows: Gastric residuals, mild distension, occult blood
Absent bowel sounds, definite tenderness, edema

steps.tx: The pathognomonic radiological hallmark of necrotising enterocolitis is **pneumatosis intestinalis appearance**. Plain abdominal radiographs demonstrate linear or bubbly gas collections tracking within the subserosal or submucosal layers of the bowel wall, caused by gas-producing bacteria invading the mucosa. Branching gas in the portal vein signifies advanced intramural bacterial fermentation.
steps.say: Pneumatosis intestinalis demonstrates gas inside the bowel wall and confirms necrotising enterocolitis.

right.title: Perforation Signs
points: Rigler sign (both sides of bowel wall visible)

steps.tx: Radiological evaluation of the neonatal abdomen in suspected necrotising enterocolitis identifies pathognomonic gas distribution within compromised bowel loops. The hallmark **pneumatosis intestinalis radiograph** demonstrates linear or curvilinear gas tracking along bowel wall submucosa, accompanied by branching gas within the portal venous system. Pneumoperitoneum presenting as a subdiaphragmatic crescent on cross-table views signifies intestinal perforation.
steps.say: Pneumatosis intestinalis radiograph demonstrates intramural bowel gas and branching portal venous gas, signalling severe necrotising enterocolitis.

vis.alt: Neonatal abdominal radiograph showing pneumatosis intestinalis with intramural gas alongside histology of mucosal coagulative necrosis.
vis.caption: Neonatal abdominal radiograph showing pneumatosis intestinalis with intramural gas alongside histology of mucosal coagulative necrosis, transmural ischemic injury, and bacterial infiltration. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Medical management requires immediate cessation of enteral feeds, decompression of the stomach with a wide-bore nasogastric tube, fluid resuscitation, and **broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics**. Regimens combine ampicillin, an aminoglycoside like amikacin, and metronidazole to cover enteric Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and anaerobic organisms for ten to fourteen days.
steps.say: Medical treatment requires gut rest, nasogastric suction, and broad-spectrum antibiotics for two weeks.

rows: Halts bacterial substrate and allows mucosal healing
Replogle or sump tube to low suction
Treats systemic and mucosal polymicrobial infection

steps.tx: The absolute indication for emergency surgical intervention is **pneumoperitoneum indicating perforation**. In extremely low birth weight neonates too unstable for laparotomy, bedside peritoneal drainage under local anesthesia stabilizes the infant. In stable infants, exploratory laparotomy with resection of necrotic bowel and creation of an enterostomy is the definitive surgical procedure.
steps.say: Intestinal perforation demands emergency surgery, using bedside peritoneal drainage or laparotomy.

left.title: Bedside Peritoneal Drainage
points: Indications: ELBW under 1000g in septic shock
Performed in NICU under local infiltration
Decompresses abdominal cavity and drains pus
